As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for banning students' use of mobile phones throughout the entire school day.

The new school year has started, and support for banning iPhone use in classrooms continues to rise

Yes, it is still July, but summer vacation has somehow already come to an end for some reason. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive year that summer break has ended before August.

Apple is ushering in the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase designated Mac and iPad products before August 27 can receive a gift card worth up to $150. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

While back-to-school promotions are certainly popular, the use of smartphones by students on campus is increasingly becoming unacceptable.

Featured comment from netizen GreenPizza

I have not seen any data supporting that student smartphone use reduces the risk of school shootings. The reality is that classroom distractions have decreased, allowing schools to fulfill their original educational mission.

A new survey by Pew Research Center shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Currently, only 18% oppose classroom bans.

Support for stricter, all-day bans from class to dismissal has risen even more sharply. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose banning student phone use throughout the entire school day.

The report also noted that support for classroom and all-day bans remains lower among younger age groups, but since 2024, support rates have risen across all age brackets. Click here to read the full report.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use only in classrooms, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
